elements.quote: Background: Whether acupuncture is effective for Bell's palsy is controversial, and potential modifiers exist according to previous studies.
elements.reason: The abstract background states the existing controversy and uncertainty about acupuncture's efficacy for Bell's palsy, but the retrieved evidence does not include a full Introduction section elaborating the current state of knowledge.

elements.quote: An overall and cumulative meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate and quantify this efficacy.
elements.reason: The abstract objectives imply the need for the review, and the Conclusion notes more well-designed RCTs are needed, but the importance/need for the review is not explicitly argued in a dedicated rationale statement.

elements.quote: Our study revealed a more convincing positive association between acupuncture and treatment of Bell's palsy, because we contained new researched literature published after 2009 which previous studies did not, and we conducted a cumulative meta-analysis trial according to chronological order.
elements.reason: Previous meta-analyses are cited ([15, 18] in text_2/text_12) and the Discussion explains how the current review differs from prior ones (new literature, cumulative meta-analysis), but this justification appears in the Discussion rather than a formal Introduction rationale.

elements.quote: The mechanism of acupuncture treatment could be explained in terms of neurology [55] and microcirculation theories [53, 54] such as activation of receptors, transmission of signals along afferent nerve fibers, projecting into central nervous systems, efferent control mechanisms, improving microcirculation, elimination of inflammation, absorption of edema, strengthening the body resistance and so on.
elements.reason: A proposed mechanism of action for acupuncture is described, but only in the Discussion, not in the Introduction/rationale section.
No logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

No retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or research question. The retrieved chunks cover methods, results, and limitations, but none states the objective explicitly.

Although this is a review of intervention effects (acupuncture vs control for Bell's palsy), no PICO-formulated statement of planned comparisons is present in the retrieved evidence; only outcome measures (RR for total effective rate/cured rate) are described in text_5, without an explicit PICO comparison statement.

elements.quote: All studies used total effective rate as an outcome measure. Only one RCT referred to adverse effects and/or complications during acupuncture [47].
elements.reason: Outcome domains (total effective rate, cured rate, course of cured patient, adverse effects) are identifiable only from the Results section; they are not listed and defined in the Methods as required, and definitions of efficacy are not provided (the authors even note 'definitions of efficacy in different studies varied').
No time frame or time points of outcome measurement are specified for any outcome domain in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results (measures, time points, analyses) within each outcome domain were sought.
No methods for selecting which results to collect within outcome domains are described.

elements.quote: We defined total cure rate and total effective rate as our end-points.
elements.reason: Primary outcomes (total effective rate and cured rate) are identified as end-points, but this appears in the Results rather than Methods and no rationale for their prioritisation is given.

elements.quote: The following information was extracted: first author, publication year, study location, sample size, mean age, disease stage.
elements.reason: The methods list some extracted variables (first author, publication year, study location, sample size, mean age, disease stage), but this list is incomplete relative to the data actually collected and used, e.g., acupuncture type, comparison interventions, efficacy assessment scales, therapy period, and outcomes shown in Table 1 and subgroup analyses (text_8, table_0, text_5). No description of assumptions made about missing or unclear study information is provided in the retrieved evidence. elements.quote: Seven aspects were evaluated as following: 1) Selection bias: random sequence generation, allocation concealment; 2) Performance bias: Using blind method to researchers and subjects; 3) Detection bias: The evaluation results of the study by the method for the blind; 4) Attrition bias: The data results integrity; 5) Reporting bias: Report the results of the study selectively; 6) Other bias...
elements.reason: The domains and components assessed (selection, performance, detection, attrition, reporting, other bias) are explicitly specified.

elements.quote: The 'high', 'moderate', 'low' was allocated for each item.

elements.quote: relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was considered as common measure of the association between acupuncture therapy and total effective rate or total cured rate
elements.reason: The effect measure (RR with 95% CI) is explicitly specified for both outcomes (total effective rate and cured rate) used in the synthesis.

elements.quote: relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was considered as common measure of the association
elements.reason: RR is used throughout for all outcomes; no re-expression of results into another effect measure is described or needed, and no evidence suggests any re-expression was performed.

elements.quote: Two investigators (Fu-ming Wang and Sha-sha Yu) independently selected the suitable publications according to following inclusion criteria: (1) Participants: subjects diagnosed with Bell's palsy. (2) Intervention: manual acupuncture or electric acupuncture. (3) Control: other therapy regimens except acupuncture. (4) Outcome: Adjusted risk estimates with 95% confidence interval (CI) on the association of acupuncture and efficacy of Bell's palsy included cured rate and effective rate. (5) Study design: RCTs.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes general eligibility criteria and independent study selection, and text_5 outlines planned syntheses (subgroups by age, design, sample size, etc., plus sensitivity and cumulative analyses). However, it does not describe the process used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis (e.g., tabulating study intervention characteristics and comparing them against the planned groups for each synthesis).

elements.quote: The percentage of cured was called cure rate, and the percentage of markedly effective or effective were called total effective rate.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes some data preparation: outcome definitions (cure rate and total effective rate derived from the House-Brackmann grading, text_3) and choice of effect measure (RR with 95% CI as common measure, text_5). However, no methods are reported for handling missing summary statistics or for data conversions/calculations (e.g., deriving RRs from reported counts), so the description is incomplete.

Tables (e.g., Table 1 'Characteristics of 20 eligible RCTs', Table 2 for subgroup analyses, Supplementary Table 1) appear in the manuscript, but the Methods section contains no description of the tabular structures used to display results or the data included in them.

Figures such as the PRISMA flow diagram and supplementary sensitivity analysis plots are shown, but the Methods never describe the graphical methods (e.g., forest plots, cumulative meta-analysis plots) used to display results of individual studies or syntheses.

No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs is reported. The only ordering statement concerns cumulative meta-analysis ('added 1 at a time in order of year of publication'), which is a synthesis procedure, not an ordering rule for tables or graphs.

No non-standard graphs are identified in the manuscript; standard outputs (flow diagram, forest-style sensitivity plots, risk of bias summary) are used, so no rationale for non-standard graphs is required.

elements.quote: All analyses were conducted using STATA version12.0 (StataCorp, College Station, TX) and RevMan 5.3 (The Nordic Cochrane Centre, Copenhagen, Denmark).

elements.quote: A random-effect model [20] was used to pool RRs to obtain the overall effect size.

elements.quote: relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was considered as common measure of the association between acupuncture therapy and total effective rate or total cured rate. A random-effect model [20] was used to pool RRs to obtain the overall effect size.

elements.quote: The between-study heterogeneity was assessed by Q statistic ( P Heterogeneity <0.10 suggesting statistically significant) and the I 2 [21] (high heterogeneity, I 2 ≥75%; moderate heterogeneity, 50.0%<I 2 <75%; low heterogeneity, I 2 <50% [22]).
